messages:
alex: quick follow-up on the GQA/MQA kernel interface RFC — i pushed a short proposal for a minimal refactor to the kernel API. want to surface tradeoffs and rollout plan before we lock it in.

maria: saw it, skimmed. high-level: sounds good to me if we keep the compatibility shim for 3 months. what's the biggest risk you see?

alex: biggest risk is subtle perf regressions when the grouped-query path hits the new kernel selector. we need a deterministic canary (single-customer) + synthetic load tests.

jamal: agree. also concerned about the extra allocations in the new selector when converting query groups -> kernel descriptors. did you measure allocs?

alex: yes — on a 16-token median seq test, allocations went +6% for gqa path. CPU headroom dropped a bit but latency p50 unchanged. p99 had a few spikes under extreme fanout.

priya: can we avoid allocations by reusing a descriptor pool? that would keep the API ergonomic but low alloc.

alex: proposal includes a DescriptorPool that's thread_local and an optional reuse flag: reuse_descriptors: true/false. default true in Dedicated/Private, false in Hosted until we validate.

lin: about the API boundary — where does kernel selection live? runtime or per-model adapter? i prefer runtime-owned selector so we can change heuristics without model changes.

maria: runtime-owned seems right. but we need a clear model manifest field for "compatibility hints" (e.g., supports_grouped_query: bool) so selector can short-circuit.

alex: agreed. manifest hint used only as a fast-path, selector still validates at runtime. fallback ordering still config-driven. example config: 
```
kernels: 
  selector: "policy-v2"
  policies:
    policy-v2:
      priority: ["gqa_k32","mqa_k8","scalar_k"]
      allow_prefix_cache: true
```

sophie: how will rollbacks work if we see quality regressions? we must have per-route override and immediate fallback to previous kernel.

alex: built-in fallback already exists. plan: deploy selector in canary with a per-route opt-in. if quality/latency degrade, ops can toggle route.override_kernel = "legacy" which instantly switches path.

jamal: telemetry — what do we need? per-token latency by kernel, KV cache hit rate by kernel, and a new "selector_decision" tag exported to traces. plus counters for descriptor_allocs and reuse_hits.

priya: add a small eval harness that replays production traces through both old and new selector to find decision divergence before rollout. can run offline nightly.

maria: agree. add an automated gate in CI that rejects changes increasing allocations >10% or p99 latency >5% on the replay harness.

lin: thoughts on test coverage: unit tests for selector heuristics, integration tests for fallback/rollback, and a small e2e perf test in release pipeline.

alex: noted. i will draft a rollout checklist: (1) descriptor pool + reuse opt-in behind feature flag, (2) selector smoke in staging, (3) replay harness pass, (4) canary on 2 customers, (5) monitor metrics for 48h, (6) broad roll.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: staging/selector-v2 -> 2026-04-02T03:00Z (dry-run).

sophie: one more UX ask — add observability in Console to show which kernel served each request (small column). product and SRE will use that for postmortems.

alex: good call. will add selector_decision to Console timeline and a per-kernel cost estimator.

jamal: ok, i can prototype DescriptorPool tonight. priya and i can work on replay harness tomorrow.

maria: thanks alex — please send the short checklist into #eng-releases when ready and i'll own the canary signoff.

alex: thanks all. i'll post the PR and the checklist by EOD.
